subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease starts carbidopa-levodopa. Carbidopa does not cross the blood-brain barrier and reduces peripheral side effects such as nausea and orthostatic hypotension while increasing the amount of levodopa that reaches the brain.
question: Carbidopa produces these effects by inhibiting which enzyme?
explanation_correct: Carbidopa inhibits peripheral aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase, also called DOPA decarboxylase, preventing conversion of levodopa to dopamine outside the brain. Because carbidopa does not cross the blood-brain barrier, levodopa that reaches the brain is still decarboxylated to dopamine by central DOPA decarboxylase.

explanation_incorrect.A: Tyrosine hydroxylase catalyzes the rate-limiting step of catecholamine synthesis and is not inhibited by carbidopa.
explanation_incorrect.B: Dopamine beta-hydroxylase converts dopamine to norepinephrine and requires vitamin C.
explanation_incorrect.C: Catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitors such as entacapone block peripheral metabolism of levodopa, but carbidopa does not inhibit this enzyme.
explanation_incorrect.D: Monoamine oxidase B inhibitors such as selegiline reduce dopamine degradation in the brain; carbidopa does not inhibit monoamine oxidase B.

educationalObjective: Carbidopa inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase, increasing levodopa delivery to the brain and reducing peripheral dopamine effects.
